\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Bonami}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.Bonami
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This file develops the notion of $B$-reasonability of a real random variable and proves
the Bonami lemma: a Boolean function of degree at most $k$ is $9^{k}$-reasonable under the
uniform measure on the hypercube. Along the way it establishes tail and anti-concentration
bounds (including the Paley--Zygmund inequality), the average/difference decomposition of a
Boolean function over its last coordinate, and the associated moment and Fourier identities.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[$B$-reasonable random variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBReasonable}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBReasonable}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p002-b003}
Let $X\colon\Omega\to\bbr$ be a function on a measurable space, let $P$ be a measure
on $\Omega$, and let $B\in\bbr$. The function $X$ is \emph{$B$-reasonable} under $P$
when $P$ is a probability measure, $B\ge1$, $X$ is almost everywhere measurable with
finite fourth absolute moment, and
\[
\E[X^4] \le B \cdot \bigl(\E[X^2]\bigr)^2 .
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Fourth-moment tail bound for $B$-reasonable variables]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.b_reasonable_tail_bound}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.b_reasonable_tail_bound}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p003-b001,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p003-b002
}
\proofstep
  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBReasonable}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}
  {pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p002-b003}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBReasonable}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space $\Omega$ that is $B$-reasonable
and whose fourth power $X^4$ is integrable, and suppose its second moment is strictly
positive, $\E[X^2] > 0$. Then for every $t > 0$,
\[
\Pr\!\bigl[\, X^4 \ge t^4\,(\E[X^2])^2 \,\bigr] \le \frac{B}{t^4}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[$B$-reasonability from a lower bound on atom probabilities]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.min_prob_b_reasonable}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{pdf-9d1751394783-p009-b003}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.min_prob_b_reasonable}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p003-b005,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p003-b006
}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBReasonable}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite sample space with all subsets measurable, let $\pi$ be a
probability mass function on $\Omega$, and give $\Omega$ the probability measure
$P(\{\omega\})=\pi(\omega)$. For any function $X\colon\Omega\to\bbr$, if $\mu > 0$
satisfies $\mu \le \pi(\omega)$ for every $\omega \in \Omega$, then $X$ is
$(1/\mu)$-reasonable under $P$; in particular,
\[
\E[X^4] \le \frac{1}{\mu}\bigl(\E[X^2]\bigr)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Paley–Zygmund inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.paley_zygmund_ineq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.paley_zygmund_ineq}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $Z$ be a measurable real-valued random variable on a probability space that is almost surely
nonnegative and has finite first and second moments $\E[Z]$ and $\E[Z^2]$, with $\E[Z] >
0$. Then for every $\theta$ with $0 \le \theta \le 1$,
\[
\Pr\bigl[\, Z > \theta\,\E[Z] \,\bigr] \;\ge\; \frac{(1-\theta)^2\,(\E[Z])^2}{\E[Z^2]}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Anti-concentration for $B$-reasonable variables]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.b_reasonable_anticon_zero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.b_reasonable_anticon_zero}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p003-b003,

}

  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.paley_zygmund_ineq}

  {pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p003-b004}
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBReasonable, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.paley_zygmund_ineq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X$ be a measurable real-valued random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$ with
finite second and fourth moments and $\E[X^2] > 0$, and suppose $X$ is $B$-reasonable.
Then for every $t \in [0,1]$,
\[
P\bigl(\,\abs{X} > t\,\norm{X}_2\,\bigr) \ge \frac{(1-t^2)^2}{B},
\]
where $\norm{X}_2 = \bigl(\E[X^2]\bigr)^{1/2}$; equivalently, the probability that $X^2
> t^2\,\E[X^2]$ is at least $(1-t^2)^2/B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Restriction of the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$, and let
$b\in\{0,1\}$. The last-coordinate restriction of $f$ at $b$ is the function
$f_b\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ defined by $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Average over the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$. Its
last-coordinate average is the function $g\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ defined by
$g(x)=\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0)+f(x,1)\bigr)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Half-difference over the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$. Its
last-coordinate half-difference is the function $h\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ defined by
$h(x)=\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0)-f(x,1)\bigr)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering the false-restriction from average and half-difference]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast_false_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast_false_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$, and let $x$ be a point of the
$n$-dimensional Boolean hypercube. Then the restriction of $f$ obtained by fixing its
last coordinate to $\mathrm{false}$ equals the sum of the average and the
half-difference of $f$ over that coordinate:
\[
f(x,\mathrm{false}) = \frac{f(x,\mathrm{false}) + f(x,\mathrm{true})}{2} +
\frac{f(x,\mathrm{false}) - f(x,\mathrm{true})}{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering the true-restriction from average and half-difference]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast_true_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast_true_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables. For a bit
$b$, write $f_b : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ for the restriction $x \mapsto f(x,b)$ that fixes
the last coordinate to $b$, and let its average and half-difference over the last
coordinate be the functions $\tfrac12(f_0 + f_1)$ and $\tfrac12(f_0 - f_1)$. Then for
every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, the restriction fixing the last coordinate to
$\mathrm{true}$ equals the average minus the half-difference at that point:
\[
f_1(x) \;=\; \tfrac12\bigl(f_0(x) + f_1(x)\bigr) \;-\; \tfrac12\bigl(f_0(x) -
f_1(x)\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Splitting a sum over the hypercube on its last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\varphi \colon \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a
real-valued function on the Boolean hypercube of dimension $n+1$. Then the sum of
$\varphi$ over all points of the cube splits according to the value of the final
coordinate:
\[
\sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^{n+1}} \varphi(x) \;=\; \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^{n}}
\varphi\bigl((y,\mathrm{false})\bigr) \;+\; \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^{n}}
\varphi\bigl((y,\mathrm{true})\bigr),
\]
where $(y,b)$ denotes the point of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ obtained by appending the bit $b$ to
$y \in \{0,1\}^{n}$ as its last coordinate.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform weight halves with each added coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the uniform weight $2^{-n}$ assigned to each point of
$\{0,1\}^n$ satisfies \[2^{-(n+1)} = \frac{2^{-n}}{2},\] so that the uniform weight on
the cube of one higher dimension is half the uniform weight on the original cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier coefficient of the average over the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierCoeff_avgLast}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierCoeff_avgLast}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$, let $g$ be the average of $f$ over its
last coordinate — the Boolean function of arity $n$ given by $g(x) =
\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,\text{false}) + f(x,\text{true})\bigr)$ — and let $S \subseteq [n]$ be
a set of coordinates among the first $n$. Write $\iota\colon [n] \hookrightarrow [n+1]$
for the inclusion sending each of the first $n$ coordinates to itself and omitting the
last, so that $\iota(S)$ is $S$ viewed as a subset of $[n+1]$ that avoids the coordinate
$n+1$. Then the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $g$ at frequency $S$ equals the
Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $f$ at frequency $\iota(S)$: \[ \hat g(S) \;=\; \hat
f\bigl(\iota(S)\bigr). \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier coefficient of the half-difference over the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierCoeff_diffLast}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierCoeff_diffLast}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables, and let
$g\colon\{0,1\}^{n}\to\bbr$ be its half-difference over the last coordinate, given by
$g(x)=\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0)-f(x,1)\bigr)$. For every frequency set
$S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$, the Fourier--Walsh coefficient of $g$ at $S$ equals the
Fourier--Walsh coefficient of $f$ at the frequency set obtained by regarding $S$ as a
subset of the first $n$ coordinates of $\{1,\dots,n+1\}$ and adjoining the last
coordinate:
\[
  \hat g(S) \;=\; \hat f\bigl(S\cup\{n+1\}\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Expectation splits over the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_succ_eq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_succ_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformWeight_succ, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\varphi : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables, and for
a bit $b \in \{0,1\}$ let $\varphi_b : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, $\varphi_b(x) = \varphi(x,
b)$, be its restriction obtained by fixing the last coordinate to $b$. Then the
expectation of $\varphi$ under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ is the average of
the expectations of its two restrictions:
\[
  \E[\varphi] \;=\; \frac{\E[\varphi_{0}] + \E[\varphi_{1}]}{2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A fourth-power sum-and-difference identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourth_pow_sum}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourth_pow_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For all real numbers $a$ and $b$, the sum of the fourth powers of $a+b$ and $a-b$
satisfies
\[
(a+b)^4 + (a-b)^4 = 2\left(a^4 + 6\,a^2 b^2 + b^4\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Parallelogram identity for real numbers]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.second_pow_sum}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.second_pow_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For all real numbers $a$ and $b$, the identity \[(a+b)^2 + (a-b)^2 = 2\,(a^2 + b^2)\]
holds.
\end{lemma}

Let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables, and let $g$
and $h$ be the average and the half-difference of $f$ over its last coordinate, so that
$g(x) = \tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0) + f(x,1)\bigr)$ and $h(x) = \tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0) -

measure, the fourth moment of $f$ decomposes as
\[
\E[f^4] \;=\; \E[g^4] + 6\,\E[g^2 h^2] + \E[h^4].
\]
\end{lemma}

Let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables. Define its
average and half-difference over the last coordinate as the functions on $n$ variables
\[
g(x) = \tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0) + f(x,1)\bigr), \qquad h(x) = \tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0) -
f(x,1)\bigr).
\]
Then, with the expectation on the left taken under the uniform measure on
$\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ and those on the right under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$, the
second moment of $f$ decomposes as
\[
  \E\bigl[f^2\bigr] = \E\bigl[g^2\bigr] + \E\bigl[h^2\bigr].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cauchy–Schwarz for the uniform expectation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_cs_sq}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_cs_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $g, h : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be Boolean functions, and let $\E[\,\cdot\,]$ denote the
expectation under the uniform measure on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$. Then
\[
  \bigl(\E[g^2 h^2]\bigr)^2 \;\le\; \E[g^4]\cdot\E[h^4].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the mean square]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_nonneg}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{1}
For every Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the expectation of $f^2$ under the
uniform measure is nonnegative: $0 \le \E[f^2]$, where $\E[f^2] =
2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n} f(x)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the expectation of a product of squares]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_nonneg_prod}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_nonneg_prod}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{1}
For any two Boolean functions $g, h : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the expectation of the
product of their squares under the uniform measure is nonnegative:
\[
\E\!\left[\,g^2\, h^2\,\right] \;=\; 2^{-n} \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} g(x)^2\, h(x)^2
\;\ge\; 0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of the fourth moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_fourth_nonneg}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_fourth_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_nonneg_prod, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean hypercube. Then its
fourth moment under the uniform measure is nonnegative:
\[
  \E\!\left[f^4\right] \;=\; 2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n} f(x)^4 \;\ge\; 0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Averaging over a coordinate preserves the degree bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_avgLast}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_avgLast}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_boolCube_succ, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables, and suppose
$f$ has degree at most $k$; that is, every set $S$ with nonzero Fourier coefficient
$\hat f(S)\ne 0$ satisfies $\abs{S}\le k$. Form the average of $f$ over its last
coordinate, the function on $n$ variables obtained by fixing that coordinate to each of
its two values and averaging,
\[
  x \;\longmapsto\; \tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0) + f(x,1)\bigr).
\]
Then this averaged function also has degree at most $k$: each set $S$ with a nonzero
Fourier coefficient of the average satisfies $\abs{S}\le k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Degree bound for the half-difference over the last coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_diffLast}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_diffLast}

\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierCoeff_diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of degree at most $k$, meaning
that every frequency set $S$ with nonzero Fourier--Walsh coefficient $\hat f(S)\ne 0$
satisfies $\abs{S}\le k$. Write $f_0$ and $f_1$ for the two restrictions of $f$ to
$\{0,1\}^{n}$ obtained by fixing its last coordinate to $0$ and to $1$ respectively, and
let $g=\tfrac12(f_0-f_1)$ be the half-difference of $f$ over that coordinate. Then $g$
is a Boolean function on $\{0,1\}^{n}$ of degree at most $k-1$, with $k-1$ interpreted
as $0$ when $k=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Degree-zero Boolean functions are constant]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_zero_const}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_zero_const}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of degree at most $0$; that is, every set
$S$ with nonzero Fourier--Walsh coefficient $\hat f(S)\ne 0$ satisfies $|S|\le 0$. Then
$f$ is constant: for every point $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ one has $f(x)=f(x_0)$, where $x_0$ is
the all-$\mathtt{false}$ point.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourth moment of a degree-zero Boolean function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_zero_fourth_moment}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_zero_fourth_moment}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.degree_zero_const, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.has_degree_at_most, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of degree at most $0$, meaning that every
set $S$ with a nonzero Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)\ne 0$ satisfies $|S|\le 0$. Then,
with expectations taken under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \E[f^4] \;=\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Algebraic inductive step for the Bonami lemma]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.bonami_algebra}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.bonami_algebra}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
\proofsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p005-b001}
Fix a natural number $m$, and let $a, b, B, C$ be nonnegative real numbers and $A$ a
real number satisfying $A \le 9^{m+1} a^2$, $B \le 9^m b^2$, and $C^2 \le A B$. Then
\[
A + 6C + B \le 9^{m+1}\,(a+b)^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

k$. Writing $\E$ for the expectation under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$, we then
have

  \E[f^4] \;\le\; 9^{k}\,\bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2.
\]

\begin{lemma}[Moments equal expectations under the uniform law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.moment_eq_expect}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.moment_eq_expect}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity $n$, let $p$ be a natural
number, and let $P$ be a probability measure on the Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$ that
assigns to each singleton $\{x\}$ the uniform weight $2^{-n}$. Then the $p$-th moment of
$f$ under $P$ equals the expectation of $f^p$ under the uniform measure:
\[
  \int f^p \, dP \;=\; \E\!\left[f^p\right] \;=\; 2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n} f(x)^p.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Uniform measure on the hypercube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformMeasure}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube}
For every natural number $n$, the uniform measure on the Boolean hypercube
$\{0,1\}^n$ is the probability measure assigning mass $2^{-n}$ to each point.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform measure of a single point of the hypercube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformMeasure_apply}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformMeasure_apply}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.uniformMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x$ be a point of the Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^n$.
Under the canonical uniform probability measure on $\{0,1\}^n$, the measure of the
singleton $\{x\}$, taken as a real number, equals the uniform weight $2^{-n}$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{3}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function whose Fourier expansion has degree at
most $k$; that is, every nonzero Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ is supported on a set
$S$ with $\abs{S} \le k$. When $\{0,1\}^n$ is equipped with the uniform probability
measure, $f$ is $9^k$-reasonable: its fourth moment is controlled by the square of its
second moment via
\[
\E[f^4] \le 9^k \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}
